lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 158: renaming a file in place no longer crashes Thunar.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request one fifty-eight: renaming a file in place no longer crashes Thunar.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
A rename starts on the main thread, from F2, the rename dialog, Properties, or undo and redo.
The job now keeps the file's location, read right there on the main thread.
Then the main thread marks the file as renaming, so a delete or reload for it is held until the swap.
On the worker thread, the job renames the file on disk and reads its new details.
It hands them to the main thread, and waits until the main thread is done.
The main thread clears the mark and swaps in the new location and details.
Then the row redraws, the undo entry for Ctrl+Z is recorded, and the file reloads if anything was held.
lines.say: Then the row redraws, the undo entry for Control Z is recorded, and the file reloads if anything was held.

lines.caption: On 26 November, Thunar crashed right after an in-place rename, reading a file's details that had already been freed.
lines.say: On November twenty-sixth, Thunar crashed right after an in-place rename, reading a file's details that had already been freed.

lines.caption: The rename job swapped those details in the background while the window drew the row; now the drawing thread swaps them.
Each file's details live in one shared object that nothing locks, so only the main thread, which reads it, may replace it.
The catch: once renamed on disk, watchers report the old name deleted, so the file is marked and such events are held.
Step 1: every rename except the bulk renamer starts this job, which now stores the file's location from the main thread.
Step 2: first, on the main thread, the file is marked; while marked, a destroy or reload only sets a second, held flag.
Step 3: the worker renames the real file and reads its new details, so slow disk work stays off the drawing thread.
Step 4: the hand-over blocks the worker until the main thread has run, so steps 5 and 6 finish before the job does.
Step 5: the main thread clears the mark, learns if anything was held, and swaps the details; a failed rename reloads instead.
Step 6: the row redraws, the undo entry is logged, and if anything was held, a reload lets a real deletion land.
Before, the worker freed the old details and loaded new ones; a draw at that moment read freed memory.
Now the worker renames on disk and reads the new details, and the main thread, which does all the drawing, swaps them in.
In between, the mark holds off Thunar's watchers, so the swap finds the same live object; one reload afterwards catches up.
In the code, the worker marks the file, renames it and reads its details; the callback clears the mark, swaps, and reloads if held.
The bulk renamer drops an unused option and reuses the new swap; Properties now ignores Enter while its rename runs.
The PR changes the rename job and the file code, which now hold events, plus Properties and the bulk renamer, and adds a test.
To undo it, revert its one commit on main; it changes no settings or saved data.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It was built and tested at the commit before CI's last fix, which only CI builds and tests.
It follows the issue's analysis, which put the crash on the main thread, reading freed file details.
Exo's source confirmed that the hand-over to the main thread makes the worker wait.
And Thunar's folder monitor already swaps a renamed file's details on the main thread.
The first version renamed on the worker and handed the swap to the main thread.
The local review moved reading the file's location to the main thread, when the job is created.
CI's review found seven things; the serious one: a watcher could destroy the file between the rename and the swap.
CI's own fix moved the whole rename onto the main thread, making the window wait on the disk.
The owner chose to keep the disk work on a worker, as the issue planned, and close the gap with the renaming mark.
That commit was built cleanly and installed in the cloud container.
On that build, the smoke test passed, and the existing in-place rename test passed.
The new test did 30 renames in a row: Thunar kept running, and Ctrl+Z undid the last one.
lines.say: The new test did thirty renames in a row: Thunar kept running, and Control Z undid the last one.

lines.caption: Then 10 renames from one Properties dialog, which closes if its file is destroyed; it stayed open.
lines.say: Then ten renames from one Properties dialog, which closes if its file is destroyed; it stayed open.

lines.caption: Reading exo's source showed the worker waits for the main thread.
Earlier designs passed CI's build and two tests, and their screenshots passed visual verify.
Not run: the rename dialog, redo, remote folders, and a memory-checking build that would catch the bug for certain.
The local code review at high found 6 things, fixed 1 and left 5.
The fix: the job now takes the file's location on the main thread, instead of reading it on the worker.
Left at first: an unconfirmed monitor case, and a pause on slow drives that the final design removed.
An unused option, left at first, is gone too; the last two were this page and a ruled-out case.
CI's first review, at high, found R1 to R7; its reviews of the final design found R8 to R11, then R12 to R15.
lines.say: C I's first review, at high, found R one to R seven; its reviews of the final design found R eight to R eleven, then R twelve to R fifteen.

lines.caption: R1, the serious one, is fixed by the renaming mark.
lines.say: R one, the serious one, is fixed by the renaming mark.

lines.caption: R2 is covered, since the file can't be destroyed mid-rename, and R3 wasn't a bug.
lines.say: R two is covered, since the file can't be destroyed mid-rename, and R three wasn't a bug.

lines.caption: R4 and R5 are fixed: the worker reads the details, and the undo entry is logged on the main thread.
lines.say: R four and R five are fixed: the worker reads the details, and the undo entry is logged on the main thread.

lines.caption: CI fixed R6 in Properties, and R7's unused option and copied code are gone.
lines.say: C I fixed R six in Properties, and R seven's unused option and copied code are gone.

lines.caption: R8: a deletion during the rename was thrown away; CI's fix holds it and reloads the file after the swap.
lines.say: R eight: a deletion during the rename was thrown away; C I's fix holds it and reloads the file after the swap.

lines.caption: R9 to R15 are accepted, not fixed: all are low, none confirmed by CI's verifier, and Review-accept trailers close them.
lines.say: R nine to R fifteen are accepted, not fixed: all are low, none confirmed by C I's verifier, and review accept trailers close them.

lines.caption: Each lasts a moment too short to matter, repeats an older behaviour, or was disproved by CI's verifier.
lines.say: Each lasts a moment too short to matter, repeats an older behaviour, or was disproved by C I's verifier.

lines.caption: Every finding is in the PR's code review comment.
CI's build and tests on the final head, which has CI's fix, have no result yet.
Visual verify checks the screenshots of each of those CI runs.
Before the merge, the head that merges runs all 36 tests; that result isn't known yet.
lines.say: Before the merge, the head that merges runs all thirty-six tests; that result isn't known yet.

lines.caption: Since the race depends on timing, only everyday use after the merge shows the crash is gone.
To see it yourself, open the issue, the PR with its checks and CI comments, and CI's first review run.
Part 3. What comes later: nothing depends on issue 157.
lines.say: Part 3. What comes later: nothing depends on issue one fifty-seven.

lines.caption: This PR fixes the crash, and no open issue builds on it yet.
An unrelated GTK warning logged before the crash wasn't traced, and this PR leaves it alone.
lines.say: An unrelated G T K warning logged before the crash wasn't traced, and this PR leaves it alone.

lines.caption: In short: the worker renames on disk, and the main thread swaps the file's details, so drawing and renaming can't collide.
